summary.intent: Build a product for the START Hack Munich Lio challenge 'Keep the Line Running': an agent that analyzes Soony's launch data, detects contradictions between documents and SAP, and takes real supplier actions, with a calm decision UI and general applicability to other companies.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses the Sunday 20:00 launch despite an all-ok plan, and shipped a polling pipeline, paper-check, anchored evidence, routines, voice decisions and Today/Plan UI on branch jonas/today-flow. Generalized the delivery site to come from master data. The Launch page builder is still running and 10 commits await a push approval.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Files are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 per file.
Challenge data is confidential: keep it in gitignored data/ and never commit it. Approving cards on real data sends real supplier emails, so tests and checks must mock sends.
Team workflow requires Entire hooks and PROGRESS.md claims. Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, and it needs per-agent hook approval (Codex).
Routines are recipes compiled to sandbox code with a fixed money/plan guard. Legacy code-only routines cannot render a diagram and were backed up and removed.
Soony-specific wording ('trucks', 'Hamburg') was hardcoded in UI and paper check; the delivery site now comes from sites.csv and the cutoff name should become per-customer data.
Voice decisions are now two-step: prepare_decision returns a one-time token and summary, and decide requires that token plus confirmed. Existing tests that call decide directly had to be updated.

code.finding: Added prepare_decision and token-gated decide (TOKEN_TTL_S=600, tokens stored in voice_tokens.json) so voice cannot approve without a confirmed yes.
The reader put the part number in `item`, so a fallback key (material_id or item or supplier_part_no) was needed. Counting arrivals brought the game-card gap from 34,800 to 6,800.
New routines and agent drafts default to mode 'ask'. A new /api/routines/suggestions endpoint surfaces decisions repeated at least twice without a routine.
Delivery site is now derived from sites.csv instead of a hardcoded 'Hamburg'.

workflow: Parallel subagents for UI builders worked well but need clear file ownership. A broken compile from one builder blocks the live rebuild for the others.
A subagent cross-check of all order confirmations and scans surfaced discrepancies (80,000 vs 8,000 art books) that a plain data read missed.
Screenshot scripts with all non-GET requests mocked let UI be verified safely against the live app.

friction: Redundant UI views (Flow/Steps/Expanded, and Today vs Plan) needed several rounds of consolidation.
Voice assistant announced a summary and then decided immediately without waiting for a yes.
Subagent-built UI changes overlapped in files, delaying rebuilds and commits.
The summary only showed the old zsh `$var:` modifier issue and a stray .vite/ cache folder as small annoyances.
Voice flow could not be tested end to end because no microphone was available in the checks.
open_items: Push the ~10 local commits to jonas/today-flow (needs user approval) and decide whether to open a PR into main and close PR #5.
Finish the Launch page replacing Plan, and the Today list with folded groups.
Make the cutoff label ('trucks') a per-customer setting in the UI.
Test the voice two-step flow with a live call.
Register sender emails in the portal and send the Karton Nowak art book order (offer valid 24 h) plus the Boise reply.
Write the README section, demo script, video and deck for the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
Delete or keep the old Claude Docs findings doc and the interview doc.
